subject: Micro-trial addendum: sprint credits vs. timebox top-up
messages:

Cc: contracts@pathfinder.ai
Date: 2027-05-08T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Short run add-on / discount ask for micro-trial

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the intro and the demo last week — the team loved the latency profile. We have one quick ask as we decide whether to extend the micro-trial. Our Q2 pilot window is compressed: can we either add 2000 additional inference minutes over the next 3 weeks, or (preferably) get a 20% credit on additional usage if we top up post-trial?

Pathfinder typically anchors on either fixed timebox add-ons (simple for procurement) or a short-term credit stack if we extend the evaluation. Which is easier on your side from a legal/finance perspective? Also cc'd contracts in case this needs a simple addendum.

Appreciate it — Samir

--
Samir Patel
Head of ML Ops, Pathfinder AI
samir@pathfinder.ai
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: contracts@pathfinder.ai
Date: 2027-05-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short run add-on / discount ask for micro-trial

Samir — thanks for the clear ask and glad the demo resonated. Short answer: we can do either, but there are trade-offs.

Option A — Timebox add-on (2000 minutes): simple amendment, charged at our trial uplift rate (listed below). Procurement-friendly, no impact to your post-trial pricing tiers.

Option B — Credit top-up (20% credit on additional usage right after trial): requires a short billing credit agreement but preserves a cleaner conversion motion (you pay less only if you use it). This approach can affect the committed pricing bands if you convert to a reserved capacity deal, we typically treat credits as one-off promotional credits.

I'll loop in Finance/legal internally to confirm costs and a short addendum template. If you want me to send a draft addendum today, say the word and I'll attach it (we can do v1 with either option and the exceptions for burst capacity).

Provisional numbers (subject to final ops confirmation):
- Timebox add-on 2000 min = equivalent to ~150k tokens; list uplift rate: $0.19/min trial uplift (total ~$380)
- Credit top-up: 20% credit applied to overage for the next 30 days after trial; credit applied up to $5k cap per micro-trial

What matters more to you — procurement simplicity (Option A) or cost flexibility (Option B)?

Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Short run add-on / discount ask for micro-trial — pricing/approval request

Team — Samir at Pathfinder wants either a 2000-minute add-on or a 20% post-trial credit (cap $5k). He prefers the credit route. Need quick guidance: what can we approve from AE side vs. what requires SDR/Finance approval?

My take: approve Option A up to $500 list price discount (AE discretionary) for fast close; Option B needs finance because of the credit cap and potential interference with tiered pricing if they convert to committed capacity. Thoughts?

Rishi — any pushback from pricing ops if we give a 20% one-off credit and cap it at $5k?
Vanessa — if we go timebox add-on, what's the smallest paperwork path to get a signed doc by the end of day?
Mateo — ops: can you confirm we can provision 2k minutes in the 1-3 day window and whether burst capacity applies?

Thanks,
Olga

Olga / team — quick notes from pricing ops:
- Option B (20% credit) is doable as a promotional credit. Finance prefers credits as a one-time line item rather than altering list rates. We should document the cap ($5k) and expiry (30 days from trial end).
- Approvals: AE can sign off on a timebox add-on up to $1,000 list discount without legal; beyond that we need the standard addendum signed by finance/legal. For credits > $2k we like to sign off in HubSpot as a promo code attached to the deal.
- Operational risk: credits applied post-trial can complicate committed-tier calculations; include a clause that credits do not count toward reserved capacity commitments.

If Olga wants to send the addendum, I'll pre-pop the finance promo code so we can track it.

Rishi
